summary: Hooy-Program's demo for the stock 48K ZX Spectrum, coded by Hellboj and Szuwarek with music and graphics by Yerzmyey and graphics by Aki. It placed 2nd in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2010.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2010, it was built specifically for the original 48K machine rather than later Spectrum models, with AY music from Yerzmyey.

summary: A small C64 demo by Dekadence, with code and music by BriteLite and graphics by Bracket. It placed 12th in the C64 demo compo at KozMOS 2012.
why: Sceners singled out its colour fades, clean design and graphics, along with the moving 2x2 hires text plotter. One later commenter called it underrated.

quote.text: Spectacular color fades! Fresh design and gfx.

summary: A Plus/4 demo by Legion Of Doom, coded by Csabo, themed on the Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics and released in February 2010.
why: A themed one-off from the Plus/4 scene, timed to the Vancouver Games. Its source code has been made available.

summary: JAC!'s Atari 8-bit demake of an "old cranky style" Amiga intro, with graphics by Rebb and music by Premium. A 12K intro that placed 7th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014.
why: A tribute that recreates a classic Amiga intro style on the Atari 8-bit, built as a 12K intro according to the video title.

summary: A C64 music demo by 4mat of Ate Bit, made for the SFX FM Expander cartridge: an FM tune layered over SID, with a scroller explaining the player and test playback of SID songs.
why: Sceners single out the tune and how subtly it uses the FM chip, with the SID carrying the lead voices, so it still sounds good without the expander.

quote.text: Clever how the SID supplies the dominant voices (and still actually sounds OK without the expander too)!

summary: A 1994 Commodore 64 demo by The Obsessed Maniacs, with code by kb and Luke, music by kb and design and charset by Half-Elf. It's tagged as a humorous, interactive parody.
why: An interactive joke demo from a mid-90s C64 group. The one CSDb comment singles out its animation as the best part.

quote.text: the animation is really the best part

summary: A Thomson demo by Puls, with code, graphics and music all by sam. It placed second in the Other 8-bit Demo compo at Forever 2016.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2016 and a rare Thomson entry in that compo. It is tagged as a karaoke prod, and its title doubles as a sing-along line.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by chlumpie, placed 6th in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A compact Atari 2600 production with a techno soundtrack. Its source code is available, and the video carries an epilepsy warning for its flashing visuals.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum invitation intro by Neon for Lovebyte 2025, shown in the Size Coding Showcase at Inércia 2024. A blocky red heart sits above the party name, dates and web address.
why: A compact party invitation that fits the Lovebyte "Blind Date" theme and all its party details into 256 bytes on a stock 48K Spectrum.

summary: Element54's two-disk-side Commodore 64 demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2026. A four-person team: WVL on code, Hammerfist and Genius on graphics, Youth on music.
why: Sceners single out the double perspective zoom scrollers, the colourful greetings part and a soundtrack likened to a movie score. Several note how much a team of four packed in, and the source code is available.

quote.text: Every single effect is really clever, and the music and graphics really set the mood. I love it!

summary: A VIC-20 demo by K2, coded by Yago with music by AMB and graphics by guest artist James of Wrath Designs. It placed 6th in the 8-Bit Demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008.
why: A rare demo for the unexpanded-looking VIC-20 from a scene that sees few new releases, entered into a mixed 8-bit compo alongside bigger machines.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by xxl (code), Vidol (graphics) and Mister Beep (music), placed 6th in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A small, compact Silly Venture compo entry from a code, graphics and music trio, fitting its show into 16K on a stock Atari XL/XE.

summary: Atlantis and Delysid's zombie-themed C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at ATWOODS Summer Open-Air 2020, with music by DivertigO and graphics by Lobo and Mythus.
why: Sceners praise how consistently it holds its horror theme, with the music matching the mood. The opening logos, the first scroller and the credits part are the bits most often singled out.
highlights: logos moving apart at the start

quote.text: Love this one - especially the small things that make it so great. How everything fits together and the music fits the mood and theme.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum intro that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2005, with code by evilpaul, music by 4mat and graphics by Eater.
why: A compo winner at Sundown 2005, beating the other entries in the Oldskool Demo competition with a small team of three.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by R0ger and PG, with music by HardCore, that won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2019. The video title calls it a demo/invitro, and the scroller invites viewers to Flop 63 from a Czech club site.
why: It took first place in the Atari Demo competition at Forever 2019, and it doubles as an invitation to another party.
highlights: car driving towards a city skyline

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Entire Group, with code and music by Rob F. and graphics by Mellona. It won the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2010.
why: It took first place in the demo competition at ZX AAA Compo 2010, and it makes use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Neon that placed second in the Oldskool 256b Intro compo at Outline 2023: a cloud of white dots on black, framed by blocky blue and red corner patterns.
why: A podium finish at Outline shows how much a 256-byte Spectrum intro can still do. The title nods to Steven Vickers, who wrote the Spectrum ROM.

summary: Delysid's space and science-fiction themed C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at BCC Party 2017, with code by nomiStake, music by Linus and graphics by Shine.
why: Sceners praise its flow, design and care for detail, and the large amount of hand-made artwork from Shine, who also drew the PETSCII screens. Several felt it should have won the compo.

quote.text: This demo surprised me time and again with its care for detail, lots of nice tiny things to discover, great flow, slick, with decent code!

summary: OMG's C64 demo, coded and drawn by Sparta with music by Jammer, that came third in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2019. Its centrepiece is huge spheres made of vector plots, with a plasma part and a scrolling text.
why: Sceners single out the record-breaking amount of vector plots, with Dane noting one of HCL's records was smashed, plus Jammer's soundtrack. Sparta also wrote his own loader, Sparkle, for it.

quote.text: Classic demo design and super sweet sound by Jammer, but what really stands out is the spheres of course.

summary: Bonzai's Commodore 64 demo, sixth in the Lethal Display series, which came second in the demo competition at Zoo 2024. Code by Trap, Walt and Ricky, graphics by Fox and Facet, music by Metal, Laxity and DRAX.
why: A second place at Zoo 2024 from a large Bonzai line-up, with three musicians and a concept credited to Trap and Facet. The compo slide billed it under a deliberately garbled title.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum invitation demo from 2021, inviting sceners to send work to Out of Compo 2021.
why: A thin fact sheet, but it's an invitation intro from deMarche, tagged nsfw, and well received on Pouët.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo from 1992, which placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at the Light and Phenomena Easter Party that year.
why: One commenter singles out an interactive part where you steer a spaceship and the starfield moves to match.

quote.text: The best part for me is the one where you can fly the space ship and the star field moves accordingly.

summary: 0xc64's debut C64 demo, coded by Jesder with graphics by JSL and music by FeekZoid. It placed joint fourth in the Oldschool Demo compo at Syntax 2014 and takes the shape of a classic logo-and-scroller intro.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a strong first release with real oldschool feel. They single out JSL's logo and FeekZoid's music, and note how well everything fits together.

quote.text: you need no multiplexer when you have good taste!

summary: A one-file Commodore 64 demo by lft, placed 8th in the X 2026 demo compo: a PETSCII cartoon story about lemmings, with detailed hires lemmings marching across the blocky character graphics.
why: Sceners single out the storytelling and humour, calling it a narrative-driven demo of the old kind, and puzzle over how so many hires lemmings, some in the border, are on screen at once. lft later published a video explaining the trick.

quote.text: i miss narrative-driven demos of yore in general, so this almost brought me to tears (of joy). funny, heartwarming, captivating, of perfect length, 10/10.

summary: An MSX2 demo by Digital Sounds System, coded by visy with graphics by SiikiKala and Lynn and music by Alpha C. It placed 7th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018.
why: A rare MSX2 entry in a major party's oldskool compo, from a small team credited in full on the fact sheet.

summary: Agony Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at 4x4 Puke Party 1995, with code by Druid, Inco and Colabor, music by Shogoon and graphics from a large team of artists.
why: Druid describes it as the group's flagship release. Sceners point to the 4x4 3D landscape, Roder's IFLI picture, the fast-paced music and the big font, and it was voted second best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: Some nice effects, graphics and music in there. I love the big font too. Very decent demo for its day.

summary: Tristesse's 1KB intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Atari Intro compo at Forever 2012.
why: A compo winner squeezed into a single kilobyte, worth a look as a compact example of what tiny Atari XL/XE intros can manage.

summary: Censor Design's Barbie-themed C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2023, with graphics by Talent, DeeKay, Carrion and Prowler and music by Magnar Harestad and Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out the clouds, the FLI Kefrens bars, the torus with scrolling balls and Peacemaker's $d01d-split sprite stretcher, along with unusual dithered colours and the flamingo scene.

quote.text: the clouds are fantastic, the torus + scrollballs are great, but that sprite stretcher is a fxxking monster - wow!

summary: Debris's 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum, coded by Tiboh, which won the 256b intro compo at Raww.orgy 2009.
why: A compo winner in the 256-byte category, packing full-screen moving colour patterns into a tiny Spectrum program. The video title notes AY sound as well.

summary: AAA Band's ZX Spectrum demo, placed third in the ZX Spectrum Demo competition at DiHalt 2011.
why: A podium finish at DiHalt 2011, one of the main Russian Spectrum parties, from a thin fact sheet with no comments to go on.

summary: Onslaught's C64 party scroller for Syntax 2009 in Melbourne, which placed 7th in the Oldskool Demo compo: a scrolling greeting message over colour bars and graphics.
why: A small party prod made for an Australian event. The scrolltext calls it an Aussie event long overdue. It's a snapshot of the C64 scene turning up at Syntax's early editions.

summary: A one-file Commodore 64 demo by Dual Crew, with code by Zaz, graphics by Devistator and music by ne7. It placed 6th in the Old School Executable Demo compo at Sundown 2012.
why: Sceners praised the colourful logo, ne7's music and especially the DYSP scroller, which runs through the side borders and is cleanly cut at both edges, something HCL said he hadn't seen before.
highlights: DYSP scroller in the side borders

quote.text: That scroller seems to be correctly cut in both sideborders, never seen anything like that on a DYSP-scroller.

summary: Nintendo's own promotional demo for the Game Boy Color, released in January 1999 to show off the new handheld's colour screen.
why: A commercial demo rather than a scene production, made by the hardware's maker itself. It's a curiosity for anyone interested in how Nintendo pitched the Game Boy Color at launch.

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo, with code, design and music by Gasman and photography by Natbat. It placed 4th in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007.
why: An unusual Spectrum demo built around photographs, here converted into chunky, dithered colour blocks. It is also released under a Creative Commons licence.

summary: Dirty Minds' Amstrad CPC demo, coded by Optimus with graphics by CeD and Voxfreax and music by Sice. It won the CPC demo compo at Amstrad Expo 2010.
why: A compo winner at Amstrad Expo 2010, put together by a small CPC team.

summary: Antares' ZX Spectrum demo with code by Konex, graphics by Fil and music by EA. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 1999 and placed third at Chaos Constructions 999.999 the same year.
why: A compo winner at CAFe 1999 that also finished on the podium at Chaos Constructions, so it stood up well against the Russian Spectrum scene of its day.

summary: Lethargy's Commodore 64 4K intro, coded by Nicron with music by Vincenzo, which came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2026. Rows of shaded balls move and twist against a grey background.
why: Sceners point out that the SID tune takes up most of the 4K, yet the intro still looks and sounds good. The source is available too.

quote.text: Very good 4K, especially considering that the SID takes 3 of the 4 K.

summary: Defence Force's Oric demo by Dbug, who did code, graphics and music, with a Jochen Hippel tune also used. It placed third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2013.
why: A Solskogen podium finish for the Oric, made almost entirely by one person, Dbug, and released for the machine's 30th year, as the title suggests.
highlights: Oric circuit blueprints drawn on screen

summary: Eternity Industry's ZX Spectrum demo from 1999, which won the demo compo at DiHalt 1999 and placed second at Chaos Constructions 999.999 (first in the alternative results).
why: A compo winner at two Russian parties in the same year, with a large crew credited for code, graphics, 3D modelling and rendering, textures and ASCII art.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by The Atari OldSkoolerz and Computer Platform Unlimited, with music by 505, entered in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2007, where it placed 13th.
why: A small Atari 8-bit release from Breakpoint 2007's Console/Real Wild compo. The title translates as "a group of stars", and the stills show a rotating cluster of dots.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari 2600 by Ed Fries, which came second in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A second place at Silly Venture from a 128-byte VCS program, coded by Ed Fries. It shows how much the 2600 can be made to do in almost no code.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Triad, coded by Iopop with music by Dalezy, that placed third in the C64 4K intro compo at Breakpoint 2006. Minimal, monochrome animated patterns of circles and rings.
why: Sceners single out Iopop's originality and design, and how the shifting patterns and Dalezy's funky, repetitive tune work together until the whole thing turns hypnotic.
highlights: grid of pulsing circles and rings

quote.text: The way the effects and the funky repetitive tune seem to walk hand in hand, together with the strange change of patterns makes it just damn nice.

summary: Up Rough's invitation to Datastorm 2014 on the NEC PC Engine, with code by MooZ, graphics by Spot and music by Octapus. Party details scroll as text over moving rainbow-and-cloud stripes.
why: A rare demoscene production for the PC Engine, and its source code has been released. It is a well-received invitation on Pouët.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by MKM, who wrote the code. It placed 8th in the combined demo/intro compo at Sommarhack 2019.
why: A small piece of code entered against full-size demos and intros in a shared compo at Sommarhack 2019.
highlights: grey streaks falling down the screen

summary: A short SAM Coupé demo coded by Sir David, with graphics by Ziutek and music by Pyramex. It won the Other plattform Demo compo at Forever 2013.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2013 and a rare demo release for the SAM Coupé, from a small team covering code, graphics and music.

summary: Tristesse's Atari 8-bit invitation to Last Party 2017 in Opalenica, Poland, shown in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2017, where it placed 5th. Code by Mono, music by LiSU, text by Vasco.
why: An invitation for a one-off party marking 20 years since the first copy-party in Opalenica, made by a well-staffed Tristesse crew with graphics from Electron and Replay.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Outsiders, with code by apeape, graphics by Blackbear and music by Nick Roll. It came second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2018, where it was shown with a 16+ warning.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions 2018, one of the main Spectrum parties, makes it worth a look for Blackbear's pictures and Nick Roll's soundtrack.

summary: Black Mail's 1989 Commodore 64 demo Tequila Sunrise: a large hand-drawn planet-over-city picture sits above a chunky logo-font scroller, with a face emblem and the group's signature in the corner.
why: Sceners praise it as a nicely designed intro, and one commenter singles out the tune by cd/mon. Additional graphics are credited to Orc and Skyline in the comments.

quote.text: Now this is a nicely designed intro.

summary: A comeback C64 demo from Digital Excess and X-Ample Architectures, released at Evoke 2017, where it placed 8th in the Alternative Platforms compo. Code by Joachim Multermann, graphics by Björn Odendahl and Thomas Heinrich, music by Gösta Bergfeld.
why: Sceners greeted it as the return of childhood heroes after decades away. They single out its deliberately oldskool scroller style, done with care and a slick finish.

quote.text:
Very oldskool scroller style demo.
You can see however it was coded with love and looks slick.

summary: Genesis Project's Christmas greeting demo for the C64, released in December 2017: a festive picture by Mermaid of Santa, a reindeer and penguins, with a scrolltext of seasonal greetings and music by MCH.
why: A small, warm seasonal release that sceners loved for its cute pixels and catchy Christmas SID, and for seeing Papademos coding again.

quote.text: Very cute. Lovely pixels and sound, nicely put together by papademos
